We tested Schema-DAG-Guided Decomposition (SDGD), which applies greedy graph coloring on the SCS graph to assign types to low-confusability batches. While oracle routing recovers accuracy (0.802 vs.\ 0.504 single-pass), all practical routing strategies fall below the single-pass baseline, and NER decomposition amplifies false positives (F1: 0.445$\to$0.251). The bottleneck is routing accuracy rather than partitioning quality. Even with oracle routing, accuracy recovers to 0.802 but falls short of per-type baselines ({>}0.85), indicating that merge amplification---not routing quality alone---is the structural bottleneck. Union merge doubles false positives (precision: 0.56$\to$0.21); voting merge sacrifices recall. Architectures that avoid explicit merge---such as retrieval-based type selection or learned routing with non-overlapping extraction---may circumvent this bottleneck. Full protocol, results, and analysis are in Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix_sdgd}.
